"Emerald 10's" has 230,327 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of Emerald 10's's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
988.headline: What the prize table shows

990.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "LADY LUCK" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "LADY LUCK" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
990.headline: How far along this game is

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" has had no $2 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

If "$2 MILLION VAULT" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
992.headline: Five months, no top prize claimed

993.body:
The top prize count on "$5,000 Triple Play" has not moved for four months. The game still has three of six top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Today's free summary of "$5,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
993.headline: Top prizes are still left

994.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$25,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "$25,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
994.headline: Early stage or late

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has two of four top prizes left and is past the halfway point of its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Everything above about "$200,000 Triple Play" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
995.headline: Early stage or late

996.body:
"$1,000,000 Triple Play" is in the second half of its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

If you play "$1,000,000 Triple Play" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
